text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Chief Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat: Talks stalled over four points.
- Settlement security boss denies beating Arab boy to death.
- Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai: No official has said "not one inch" on Golan.
- Gesher threatens to vote against budget.
- Microsoft and local company VDOnet to offer video link on Internet.
- Bank of Israel cuts interest rates by 0.3 percentage points.
- Number two at Bank of Israel, David Klein: Slowdown is timely.
- Plans to expand Israel's main airport, Ben-Gurion 2000, will not be finished until 2001 or 2002.
- Small firms account for 60 percent of export growth.
- U.S. judge clears way for Swiss company to boost stake in InterPharm.
GLOBES
- Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel lowers interest rate by only 0.3 percentage poitns. The representative rate of the dollar fell by 0.8 percent to 3.255 shekels.
HAARETZ

- U.S. worried by deviant movement of Syrian units to activate Scud missiles. Source in intelligence unit: "There's no change in the Syrian deployment in the Golan. The activities recently -- part of routine manoeuvres."
- Discussion on budget laws and economic arrangements begin today in Knesset.
- In the Shin Bet preparations are under way for preventive arrests of right-wing extremists during the Hebron redeployment.
- Officer convicted of causing death through negligence promoted and given job of brigade commander.
MAARIV
- Senior Israeli official tells foreign journalists: "There's a fear Syria will enter into a limited war." Reports in Jordanian and Lebanese papers of Syria preparing for war.
- Israeli security forces say they seized a booby-trapped cellphone that terrorists tried to get into Israel, possibly to kill someone.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Israelis and Palestinians: No crisis, in the end we'll sign.
- A hit in Israel: Boots made of black shiny leather called "Nazi".
